doc.title: Marian McPartland interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, April 26, 1997

title: Playing for high school audiences
summary: Rowe recalls her 1974 visit to his high school; she discusses school and college dates and the Port Washington band.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: That reminds me of course I was going to get to this a little later, but we’ll go there now. Remember when you came to my high school, in 1974 I think?
And you played “Sunshine of My Life.”
Yes, you did. And of course at that time, that was a pop hit.
And the kids loved it. And I’ve often wondered, are some of those situations where you get in front of a high school audience, that they’ve been tough along the way? © Fillius Jazz Archive -4-

Not too bad, truthfully. I mean I haven’t played for a big group of like high school kids for a long time. I think depending on where they are — like if it was a New York City school, I think I would have to be armed and dangerous to be able to put over anything to those kids, but I don’t know. I haven’t been asked to do one, but it would be a challenge. But I do do quite a few high school and college dates, and I do, every year, do a thing with a high school band in Port Washington. I figure they really ought to know something about jazz since I live there, and we really have quite a good little band going now. Of course unfortunately they leave and go to college, but a lot of them have actually stayed in music. It’s quite amazing. So I do that and then different college dates. Ithaca College is one and I guess I’m going to play it again sometime later this year.
